title: Inspect cells: inquest report
article: An inquest into the death of a Pauingassi First Nation woman who hanged herself while in police custody has recommended that RCMP cells be regularly inspected to ensure they meet current safety standards.
Darlene Rose Owens, 23, died Oct. 19, 2005 after she tore her T-shirt and used it to hang herself from the doorknob of her cell.
Owens was intoxicated and causing a disturbance at her father's home when she was taken into custody by a band constable and held in an RCMP trailer used as a detention facility.
In an inquest report released yesterday, Judge Janice leMaistre made seven recommendations for improving safety in RCMP cells.

Other recommendations included improving safety and suicide prevention training for band constables responsible for detaining prisoners, increasing funding for the recruitment of guards, and regular maintenance of camera monitoring systems in cells.
